obs: Consolidated Edison Co. v. National Labor Relations Board

"We think that this authority to order affirmative action does not go so far as to confer a punitive jurisdiction enabling the Board to inflict upon the employer any penalty it may choose ... The power to command affirmative action is remedial, not punitive"
National Labor Relations Board v. Newport News Shipbuilding & Dry Dock Co.
“Sec. 10(c) was not intended to give the Board power of punishment or retribution for past wrongs or errors. Action under that section must be limited to the effectuation of the policies of the Act.”
National Labor Relations Board v. Stowe Spinning Co.
“However, it is well established by decisions of this Court that 10 (c) of the Act is remedial, not punitive.”
Gilbertville Trucking Co. v. United States
"However, as 5 (7) itself implies, the Commission's power is corrective, *130 not punitive. The justification for the remedy is the removal of the violation."
